_about: Design parameters from Szonja's sheet, contracts/sources/chip_geometry_requirements.xlsx (Sizing Calculator, Geometry Requirements, Step 1 and Step 3 tabs). 'source' lists keys from 'sources' below. 'assumption': true marks rules of thumb the sheet says are not from a paper (confirm with Ayrton). Where the sheet gives a range, 'min'/'max' hold it and 'value' is null unless the sheet names a typical value. operator/sizing.py uses the same defaults; tests/test_sizing.py checks they agree.

10x.reference: 10x Genomics CG00054 Rev B (cultured cell lines)

inDrops.reference: Harvard Single Cell Core inDrops sample prep guide

TIP-seq.reference: Bartlett et al., J Cell Biol 220, e202103078 (2021)

Assumption.reference: Design rule of thumb, not from a paper: confirm with Ayrton

Textbook.reference: Standard physics / fluid mechanics values (e.g. water viscosity at 20 C, Sampson orifice flow, rectangular-channel resistance)

capsule.diameter_um.note: CapSeq typical 70 +/- 3 um; SPC methods paper 75 +/- 1.5 um; tunable 35-260 um

capsule.diameter_tunable_um.note: Range capsules can be made in

capsule.count.note: Sheet default. CapSeq says >100,000 CELLS per run; capsules needed = cells / mean cells per capsule (sizing.py cell mode)

capsule.swell_factor.note: Capsules swell >2x during culture without bursting; occupied capsules swell, empty ones don't

capsule.mean_cells_target.note: ~0.1 cells per capsule; most capsules empty. Size chambers by capsule count, not cell count

capsule.retained_nucleic_acid_min_bp.note: Capsule permeability: >300 bp kept. No geometry impact

capsule.enzyme_pass_max_kda.note: Enzymes under ~160 kDa pass the shell. No geometry impact

capsule_channel.width_factor_low.note: Rule of thumb to avoid clogging

capsule_channel.width_factor_high.note: Rule of thumb to avoid clogging

trap.gap_factor_high.note: Rule of thumb; check_chip_spec.py errors at or above this

culture.chamber_height_min_um.note: Culture chamber height and trap clearance >= ~150 um (swollen capsules)

culture.temp_c.note: Days-weeks in medium at 37 C, 5% CO2

release.outlet_min_width_um.note: Outlet sized for released spheroids (~150 um+) after the matrix-digesting enzyme release step

size_sort.cutoff_um.note: Optional weir or DLD to drop empty (unswollen) capsules

cell_filter.gap_um.note: 10x 30 um; inDrops 40 um then 20 um; TIP-seq 30 um. Must be <= encapsulation nozzle width

cell_wash.dld_critical_diameter_um.note: Medium-exchange module replacing pelleting: DLD critical diameter ~8 um (or spiral inertial channel)

cell_wash.pellet_g.note: Bench step to be replaced: 250-300 g, 5 min, 4 C

dissociation.temp_c.note: Enzymatic dissociation reagent held at 37 C. The reagent, its concentration and the chelator it carries are not recorded in this repo (CONFIDENTIALITY.md); only the temperature matters to the chip, which needs a 37 C zone over the dissociation chamber

dissociation.outlet_min_width_um.note: Outlet wide enough for detached cells and small clumps

cellprep.mean_cells_tolerance.note: TODO placeholder: Module 1b accepts a mean of 0.1 +/- 25% cells per capsule (0.075-0.125) before handing cells to Module 2

cellprep.max_dilution.note: TODO placeholder: the most m1b_resuspend_1 can dilute in one pass

encapsulation.shell_flow_ul_h.note: Shell stream: the photocrosslinkable hydrogel precursor.

encapsulation.cell_flow_ul_h.note: Core stream: cells suspended in the viscous core buffer (see encapsulation.core_buffer_viscous)

encapsulation.core_buffer_viscous.note: FLAG, not a number: the core stream is not water. It carries a high-molecular-weight, non-ionic polymer crowding agent, which is what makes the aqueous two-phase system work: the core buffer and the shell precursor are mutually immiscible and density-matched, so each droplet phase-separates into a core inside a shell instead of mixing. ENGINEERING CONSEQUENCES, which is all this repo records: the core stream is markedly more viscous than water, so channels carrying it are made WIDER and SHORTER to keep the pressure drop down (see the Module 1b resuspension mixer), and fluid.viscosity_pa_s (water) understates the core leg of any flow calculation. The polymer, its molecular weight and its concentration are held outside this repo (CONFIDENTIALITY.md)

crosslink.photoinitiator_percent_w_v.note: Photoinitiator loading for the 405 nm cure, from the cited paper's figure; treat the exact loading as the paper's, not ours

wash.bench_g.note: Bench capsule wash, 2 min, 4 C; replaced on chip by a trap with back-flush

wash.exchange_steps_per_run.note: After lysis, reverse transcription, and the final wash

lysis.chaotropic.note: FLAG, not a number: fragile cells need a harsh lysis buffer built on a STRONG CHAOTROPIC SALT at high molarity. ENGINEERING CONSEQUENCES, which is all this repo records: (1) every wetted surface, seal and adhesive on the lysis path must be chemically resistant to it; (2) it is a potent inhibitor of every downstream enzyme, so it must be washed out of the capsules before reverse transcription, ligation or amplification - this is why the wash budget exists; (3) silica-like surfaces bind nucleic acid in it, so glass is a poor wetted surface there; (4) it needs its OWN waste port and line, and that waste must never meet bleach. The salt and its concentration are not recorded in this repo (CONFIDENTIALITY.md)

reagents.common_lines.note: Lysis, wash, protease, PCR mix, etc.

rt.temp_c.note: Typical RT temperature; exact value in CapSeq supplementary methods (not yet pulled)

pcr.max_temp_c.note: Index PCR; heater/Peltier capable of ~98 C under sublibrary chambers

ivt.time_h.note: Needs a sealed chamber against evaporation

fluid.viscosity_37c_pa_s.note: USE THIS FOR EVERY CULTURE AND PROTOCOL FLOW OR SHEAR CALCULATION. The chips run at 37 C carrying culture medium, not water at room temperature. Water at 37 C is 0.69 mPa s (textbook); dissolved protein raises it roughly 15%, giving about 0.8 mPa s. Marked an assumption because the exact medium is not characterised. Every generator originally hard-coded 0.8e-3, which was the right physics with the wrong provenance; pointing them at fluid.viscosity_pa_s (water at 20 C) instead made every derived flow 20% too conservative. Keep the two values separate.

fluid.viscosity_pa_s.note: Water at ~20 C. This is the DYE DEMO value: room-temperature water in a bench test. Do NOT use it for a 37 C culture or protocol calculation - use fluid.viscosity_37c_pa_s, which is 20% lower, or every flow you derive will be needlessly conservative. Note also encapsulation.core_buffer_viscous: the core stream is markedly more viscous than either value.

mesh.open_fraction.note: TODO: open area of the bought mesh (woven nylon is typically 30-40%); from its datasheet

mesh.bed_resistance_kpa_per_ul_min.note: TODO placeholder: flow resistance of a full capsule monolayer on the mesh. The clean mesh is negligible (operator/flow_calc.py); the capsule bed dominates. The pressure sensor refits this

capsule.escape_pressure_kpa.note: TODO placeholder: pressure across the mesh at which soft capsules start squeezing through the opening; measure on the bench

capsule.loss_rate.units: fraction per 10 s per unit overpressure
capsule.loss_rate.note: TODO placeholder: how fast capsules escape above the escape pressure (model and virtual chip)

capsule.diffusion_time_s.note: CapSeq: reagents diffuse into capsules within minutes. 60 s first-order lag is a TODO placeholder

backflush.lift_flow_ul_min.note: TODO placeholder: upward flow that lifts a capsule monolayer off the mesh

thermal.tau_s.note: TODO placeholder: first-order time constant of a Peltier stage under the chip

demo.target_fill_s.note: FILMABLE FILL TIME for the food-dye demo, per chamber. 'value' is what tools/demo_plan.py aims the chip's largest chamber at; 'min'/'max' are the window a viewer can actually read on camera - below about 10 s the chamber is full before anyone has looked at it, above about 60 s nobody watches to the end. DYE HAS NO SHEAR LIMIT: shear.culture_ceiling_dyn_cm2 is the ADHERENT-CELL ceiling and capsule.escape_pressure_kpa is the capsule limit, and neither applies to coloured water on an empty chip. The only bounds on a dye flow are this window and demo.max_drive_pressure_kpa. Holding a dye fill to the cell ceiling is what left spc_demo_v1's protocol running at 0.071 uL/min, over an hour to fill 4.68 uL, which nobody could film.

demo.max_drive_pressure_kpa.note: TODO PLACEHOLDER, NOT A MEASUREMENT. A deliberately conservative stand-in for how much pressure the bonded seal of a printed-and-embossed chip will take, used only as a ceiling on the demo drive pressure in tools/demo_plan.py. The contracts hold no bond-strength value because nobody has burst a real chip yet; when someone does, replace this with the measured figure, drop 'assumption' and say which chip and which bonding run it came from. Film- and thermally-bonded thermoplastic devices in the literature hold hundreds of kPa, so 20 kPa is about an order of magnitude inside the expected failure point. Never quote it as this chip's bond strength, and never design a flow that sits AT it.

dye.diffusivity_m2_s.note: TODO placeholder for a small-molecule dye in water; confirm from literature. Used by flow_calc's open-channel estimate (APPROXIMATE)

dye_demo.bench_flow_ul_min.note: Syringe rate for the Module 1 bench dye demo, and the key the twin and operator/module1_operator.py both read. DERIVED, not chosen: tools/demo_plan.py takes the one-pump route through module1_v1 (feed p_in, vent p_mid, everything else plugged) and picks the flow that puts the most chambers on it inside the demo.target_fill_s window - n_cx's 3.132 uL fills in about 30 s and j_mid's 1.728 uL in about 16 s - then checks the predicted drive pressure (operator/flow_calc.py at fluid.viscosity_pa_s, water at 20 C) against demo.max_drive_pressure_kpa. It comes out around 0.007 kPa, well under. Marked an assumption because the window it rests on is one. It REPLACES a bare 50 uL/min literal in module1_operator.py, at which n_cx filled in under 4 s - too fast for anyone to watch, which is the whole point of the demo. Note this is a DYE rate: no cells, so shear.culture_ceiling_dyn_cm2 does not apply and the culture feed is a different, much lower number. tests/test_demo_plan.py fails if this value and the derivation drift apart.

reservoir.default_ul.note: Starting volume of each reagent reservoir unless a scenario says otherwise

exchange.target_fraction.note: Default goal for an exchange step

exchange.interior_target_fraction.note: Goal inside the capsules (diffusion lag): the optimizer adds a no-flow soak until the capsule interior reaches this

control.pressure_margin.note: Plans must keep predicted pressure below this fraction of the escape pressure

control.error_threshold.note: Prediction error above this triggers a model update and re-plan

control.slices_per_wash.note: Executor time slices per wash (measure and correct after each)

barcoding.scheme.note: Only PLATE-BASED split-and-pool is dropped; per-CELL barcoding is not. Module 3's reverse transcription uses a plain poly(dT) primer and adds no barcode itself. The per-cell barcode comes from stage 4b (protocols/sctip_spc_v1.json): each capsule is re-injected into its own oil droplet, where one barcode from a pool of 16 random bases (4.3e9) is clonally amplified IN THAT DROPLET and overlap-extended onto that capsule's cDNA - AmpliDrop (doi:10.1101/2024.08.13.607508) on semipermeable capsules. The emulsion is the containment: no anchor, no cleavage. One capsule = one cell, so the data IS single-cell. Barcoding must follow RT, because overlap extension needs a template already inside the capsule. The per-lane label plus module 4's four sublibrary indices (~twelve groups) are DEMULTIPLEXING, not resolution, and must never be counted as the barcode space - doing so is what made this repo wrongly conclude the data was lane-level. Loading is Poisson at mean 3: ~5% of droplets get no barcode and those cells are lost; most get several and are merged computationally. Droplet hardware is bought (below the 200 um in-plane floor); the chemistry is ours.

barcoding.random_bases.note: Length of the random cell barcode, so the pool is 4^16 = about 4.3e9 sequences. This, not lanes x sublibraries, is the barcode space that sets the collision rate.

barcoding.loading_mean.note: Barcode loading is Poisson because a free molecule cannot be ordered the way a close-packed bead can. Aiming for exactly one would discard 37% of cells, so the published method runs at a mean of 3: about 5% of droplets get none and are lost, and about 80% get several and are resolved afterwards by merging barcodes that share fragments.

barcoding.lanes.note: Per-lane lipid-oligo barcodes carried by the cells: one per lineage.

shear.culture_ceiling_dyn_cm2.note: Applies to chambers holding ADHERENT CELLS, where the risk is detaching them. It does NOT apply to chambers holding CAPSULES: a capsule is not attached to anything and the limit there is capsule.escape_pressure_kpa, which the planner already enforces. m3_wash runs its back-flush and release at the lift flow, about 0.038 dyn/cm2, deliberately: below the lift flow the capsule bed does not come off the weir. Do not 'fix' that by lowering it.

shear.capsule_handling_note.note: Capsule-handling steps are bounded by escape pressure, not by the culture shear ceiling. Published adherent-cell detachment is around 0.6 dyn/cm2 (see protocols/retention_audit.md), so the 0.01 ceiling already carries a 60x margin for the chips that do hold cells.

shear.prelysis_rinse_ceiling_dyn_cm2.note: Rinse immediately before a deliberate lyse/quench, NOT a culture step. The 0.01 culture ceiling exists to keep adherent cells attached for weeks; held to it, a pre-quench rinse takes about 12 MINUTES, which perturbs metabolism for roughly 700x longer than the ~1 s quench we engineered the comb geometry to achieve. That defeats the whole point. Published adherent-cell detachment is near 0.6 dyn/cm2 (protocols/retention_audit.md), so 0.3 is half of it, applied for about 20 s to cells that are about to be killed anyway. Losing a few cells here costs nothing; a 12-minute perturbation costs the measurement.
